analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page introduces Bernoulli equation linking static and dynamic pressure, lists flow restrictions, presents macro scale energy derivation and molecular interpretation, and describes tube airfoil and pitot tube applications.

overview.headline: Bernoulli links static and dynamic pressure in steady inviscid flow

keyPoints.point: Bernoulli relation shows static pressure plus dynamic pressure equals total pressure constant throughout flow
keyPoints.quote: the static pressure plus the dynamic pressure is equal to the original total pressure in a flow

keyPoints.point: This Bernoulli form requires inviscid incompressible steady flow without heat addition and negligible height change
keyPoints.quote: the restrictions for this form are that the flow is inviscid, incompressible, steady, without heat addition, and with negligible change in height

keyPoints.point: Ordered directed motion creates dynamic pressure while random molecular motion creates static pressure
keyPoints.quote: We can associate a “pressure” with the momentum of the ordered motion of the gas.

keyPoints.point: Pitot static tube measures static and total pressure to compute velocity using Bernoulli relation
keyPoints.quote: In a pitot-static tube, we measure the static and total pressure and can then use Bernoulli’s equation to compute the velocity.

keyTerms.gloss: pressure from random molecular motion still present in flow
keyTerms.quote: The remaining random motion of the molecules still produces a pressure called the static pressure.

keyTerms.gloss: pressure linked to momentum of ordered motion of gas
keyTerms.quote: We call this pressure the dynamic pressure.

keyTerms.gloss: constant sum of static and dynamic pressure along flow
keyTerms.quote: We call this constant the total pressure pt of the flow.

keyTerms.gloss: flow where density remains constant throughout motion
keyTerms.quote: Assuming that the flow is incompressible, the density is a constant.

keyTerms.gloss: path that confines Bernoulli constant when restrictions apply
keyTerms.quote: In the integration of the general equations, an assumption was also introduced that restricts this equation to be true only along a single streamline.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Helps learners see how total pressure splits into static and dynamic parts and check trade between velocity and pressure under given restrictions
Orders macro scale steps so learners follow assumptions that turn enthalpy conservation into pressure velocity relation
componentPlan.focusQuote: We shall derive Bernoulli’s equation by starting with the conservation of energy equation.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Reinforces recall of definitions restrictions and applications before exploring pressure velocity calculations
componentPlan.focusQuote: The surface of the airfoil is a streamline.
